I always feel that Molyneux doesn't really deserve all that hate he gets. To clarify: He has performed a considerable number of blunders, and I have absolutely no problem with people calling him out for that, but I think there's a distinction between him and people like the NMS team or Tim Schafer in that Molyneux does not build up artificial hype despite of very well knowing that it won't work, but rather gets overhyped himself and ends up excited like a small puppy - only to be met with the harsh world of reality.

I think in part this behavior amongst older devs can be traced back to how (relatively) less resource-intensive game development was back then. Unreal, that big, big graphics whore of its time, was made in the garage of one of the dev's parents if memory serves. Doom had a similar background. But nowadays you need a proper office an eight people just to have nice visuals, not to speak of the gameplay etc.

I think he needs to be in a team, but not in charge. Perhaps that's what happened at Bullfrog, but lately he has been dreaming big without actually translating his ideas into coherent gameplay.

Whatever he is doing now, he was still involved in some unique and amazing games.
